scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for me to delete my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help her parents. That's a lot of responsibility, especially since I'm still a student and have my own stuff to do. I brought my Nintendo Switch with me because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute every day. That makes sense because having something to distract me during the long ride would help me relax and maybe even study a bit. My stepbrother wanted to play on the Switch, and since he's really into it, it actually helped distract him while I studied. That's a good thing because it kept him occupied and probably made the week easier for both of us. So, I created a new profile for him on the Switch so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That was a smart move because it kept my games safe and gave him his own space to play without interfering with mine. When I got back to school, I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eShop. That sounds frustrating. I mean, having to switch profiles every time you want to do something on your Switch would get annoying after a while. So, I decided to delete his profile to make things easier for myself. That seems reasonable on the surface because it simplified my routine. Now, fast forward to Thanksgiving. I brought my Switch again for the train ride to my dad's house. My stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen where I was talking with my dad. He was freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it, he started crying, not full-on crying, but his eyes were watery and red. Now he's holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knows my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my Switch over when I visit. So, was it right or wrong for me to delete his profile? Let me break this down. First, I created the profile to help him and to keep my games safe. That was considerate and responsible. But then, when I got annoyed with the profile switching, I deleted it without considering how it would affect him. That seems a bit selfish because I didn't think about his feelings or how much he might have been enjoying playing on the Switch. On the other hand, the Switch is my device, and I have the right to manage the profiles on it. I was annoyed by the constant switching, and it was affecting my experience. So, deleting the profile was a way to maintain control over my own device and ensure it worked smoothly for me. But then, when my stepbrother found out, he was really upset. He had invested time into his Zelda save, and losing it was a big deal for him. My dad also thinks it was mean, which adds another layer of criticism. So, even though I had a reason for deleting the profile, the way I handled it and the impact it had on my stepbrother make it seem like it wasn't the best decision. Maybe I should have communicated with him before deleting the profile. If I had told him I was going to delete it and why, he might have understood, or we could have found another solution together. Instead, I just deleted it without any discussion, which probably made him feel blindsided and hurt. Also, considering that I usually don't bring the Switch over when I visit, maybe I should have thought about whether it was necessary to bring it this time. If I knew it was going to cause problems, perhaps leaving it at home would have been better. But I wanted something to do during the train ride, so that's understandable. In the end, while I had reasons for deleting the profile, the lack of communication and the emotional impact on my stepbrother make it seem like it wasn't the right thing to do. It's important to consider others' feelings, especially when it comes to shared experiences like playing video games. Even though the Switch is mine, my stepbrother had a stake in it too, and I should have respected that. So, to sum it up, deleting the profile wasn't entirely wrong because I had reasons for doing it, but the way I handled it and the lack of consideration for my stepbrother's feelings made it seem mean and unfair. It would have been better to talk it through and find a solution that worked for both of us instead of just deleting it without any discussion.
